title: The Heart Goes Down
draft: Animatic draft from the written script: every mark is relative to where he falls (W); cameras unsurveyed, cast and wiring to come.

shots.note: His head and shoulders; the blow at a slow world: the last hit lands on his hood and helm (sparks, frost, fire or splinters by its school; no weapon in frame). The light in his eyes gutters. Cut on the impact.
Low at the water from the south-west: he goes down on his knees in the river; the greatsword falls from his right hand and sinks. His left arm stays up, the lamp held clear of the water, steady.
Up at him past the lamp. He looks at the lamp, not at her. W4, in another voice: a man's, tired, sixty, no boom. The arm begins to shake.

On her, his lamp's light on her face: she looks at him and nods, once, slowly. Yes. The first thing she gives anyone in the game, given to the thing that drowned her. (Devout: then the Order's sign for the dead, finger and thumb closing on the air.)
The fist lowers, and the lamp goes into the river. The flame hisses out in a puff of steam. Dark.

Low behind her: he folds forward into the water and is still. The mist closes over him. A beat of nothing. Then the water over his chest lightens from beneath. 'The Ford-Warden falls', small, at the end.
Slow push toward the light: the heart rises out of the water, a stone the size of a fist full of cold light, turning, water running off it. Its hum and the river. The lamp motif's bell.

Over her shoulder: the heart drifts toward her like a thing finding its way. Her hand comes up into frame (calling: the shield arm lowers; the cleaver rests in the water; the arcanist's fire goes small and steady; the stalker unnocks).
Side-on: her fingertips and the heart a hand's breadth apart. Its light leans toward her fingers like a flame in a draught.
The mud bursts up under her hand: Grimtunnel, up to the waist, snatches the heart out of the air and hugs it to his chest. A hard shake. G1.

From her eye height, down at him: the heart's light strains out of his arms toward her. He looks at it, up at her, at it. His head-lamp swings up into her face; two sniffs. Toad-still. His head dips: very nearly a bow. G2. Then a laugh shakes him back into himself.

G3, broken in the middle, half over his shoulder as he dives head first, still clutching the heart; the hole folds in behind him; the heart's light shows for a moment through the mud going down, then is gone.

10 m up over the north bank, 60 m east, looking west along the river: the ford small, her in it; the road's blue irons either side. Silence. Then from under everything a groan, felt in the ground; the river shivers in rings; every lamp in the frame dips at once and comes back. The sky's lowest edge has gone grey. She looks down at her feet.
She stands in the ford with the dawn coming. Pull back and up into the follow camera. Bars out. Control.
